overview.body:
**Gula** ​(*gula*) ‌— Healing, ‌Medicine ​· ​The ​great ​one — ​belongs ‌to ​the ​Mesopotamian tradition, ‌where ​it ‌is ​catalogued under ‌the ​domain ​"Healing, ​Medicine". ​The name ​means ‌"The ​great ‌one".

**Gula** ​is ‌healing, ​medicine. ‌The ​name means ‌"The ​great ​one" ‌and belongs ‌to ‌the ​mesopotamian ​tradition.

PuniCodex ‌restores ​the ​name ‌as ​**Gula** and ​serves ‌its ​temple ‌at [its ​temple](https://punicodex.com/gula/). ​The ​restoration ​needs ‌no distinctive ‌letters ​or ‌diacritics ​its ASCII ​form ‌would ‌lose, ‌which places ‌the ​name ‌in ​Tier ​2. The ​plain ‌ASCII ​form ​*gula* survives ​as ‌a ​modern ​convenience ​imposed by ‌the ​early ‌domain-name ​system; the ‌restoration, ​not ‌the ‌fallback, is ​the ​form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
The ​name ‌is ‌attested in ​Cuneiform ​as ​**𒀭𒄖𒆷**. ​Etymologically ​it means ‌"The ​great ​one".

‌The ​ASCII ‌form *gula* ​survives ‌only ​because ​the ​early domain-name ​system ​could ‌not ​carry ‌diacritics; ​it is ‌a ​technological ‌compromise, ​not ‌an ancient ​spelling. ​The ‌Unicode ‌restoration ‌**Gula** ​recovers the ​full ‌diacritic ​detail ​of ‌the scholarly ​transliteration ​directly ‌in ​the ‌address ​bar. The ​restoration ​needs ​no ‌distinctive ‌letters or ​diacritics ‌its ​ASCII ​form ‌would ‌lose, which ‌places ‌the ​name ‌in ​Tier 2.

​The ​letter-by-letter ‌transformation ​runs:

​- ​**g** → ‌**G** ​— ​Same, ​capitalized
‌- **u** ​→ ‌**u** ​— ‌Same
​- ‌**l** → ‌**l** ​— ​Same
​- ​**a** → ‌**a** ‌— ​Same

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/gula/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**gula** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Gula.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"gula" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Gula".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"gula" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Gula" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Gula was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Gula ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Gula ‌place ​healing, medicine ​at ​the ​center of ​a ‌living mythological ​world.

​### ‌Origins (Myth)

​Gula ‌appears ​in mesopotamian ‌tradition ​as healing, ​medicine. ​The ​name's meaning, ​"The ‌great ​one", shapes ‌the ​narratives told ‌about ​this ‌figure.

### ​Worship ‌and ​Memory (Cult)

​Devotees ‌and later ‌tradition-keepers ‌preserved ​Gula in ​ritual, ‌text, ​and iconography, ​ensuring ‌the name ​survived ​into ‌the modern ​scholarly ‌record.

​The myths ​of ​Gula survive ​in ‌fragments, ‌summaries, and ​later ‌retellings. ​Each version ​reflects ‌the interests ‌of ‌its ‌tellers — ​poets, ‌priests, ​philosophers, and ​scholars. ​The PuniCodex ‌entry ​does ​not privilege ​a ‌single ​version; it ​gathers ​the attestations ‌so ​that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. ​The restoration ‌Gula ‌gives the ​figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Gula ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Mesopotamian ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌𒀭𒄖𒆷, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​healing ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Gula is ‌to ​hold ​the ​idea ​of healing, ​Medicine ‌in ​the ​mind ‌and to ​ask ‌what ​of ‌it endures. ​The ​name ​means ​"The ​great one" ‌— ​and ‌a ​name that ‌carries ​its ‌meaning ​so ‌openly invites ​meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere ‌recollection. The ​tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name as ​healing, ‌Medicine ​· ​The ‌great one.

​Sit ‌with ​the ​restored ​form — ​Gula ‌— ‌and ​the diacritics ‌themselves ​become ​the ‌practice: ‌each mark ‌is ‌a ​small ‌act ​of attention, ​a ​refusal ‌to ​let the ​plain ​ASCII ‌form ​*gula* ​stand in ​for ‌the ​whole. ‌What the ​tradition ‌preserved ​in ‌this ‌name, the ​restoration ​asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
